facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: ATS Corporation entered Q2 FY2027 with a moderately levered balance sheet that is drifting the wrong way. The company's own measure, net debt to pro forma adjusted EBITDA, rose from 2.8x at March 31, 2026 to 3.1x at September 27, 2026, because trailing twelve month adjusted EBITDA fell while net debt rose, helped along by a share repurchase of 61.3 under the normal course issuer bid. Management now expects to operate above its 2.0x to 3.0x target range for the rest of FY2027. Earnings pressure is volume driven: six month FY2027 revenues fell 7.2% year over year (1,359.5 against 1,465.2) and Q2 FY2027 revenues fell while Order Bookings rose, so backlog of 2,009 supports near-term revenue but at a lower margin. Debt service looks comfortable on cash interest cover of 4.18x for the trailing twelve months, and liquidity is large relative to the debt wall: the senior secured revolver runs to December 2029, and the first large principal maturity on the disclosed instruments is the U.S. dollar senior notes in December 2028. The quality of the numbers deserves care. Cash flow in FY2026 was flattered by a large working capital release, adjusted EBITDA adds back restructuring charges that recur every year, the covenant tests are described but not quantified, the interim statements arrive without notes, and management reports a material weakness in internal control. The view is therefore moderate leverage, strong liquidity, deteriorating earnings and incomplete covenant evidence.

The trailing twelve month pro forma figure equals the sum of the last four quarters of adjusted EBITDA, so no pro forma acquisition uplift is visible in recent periods (C5). facts.text: Operating cash flow is dominated by working capital timing. rows.label: ATS has ample liquidity and no large principal maturity before December 2028, but earnings are falling and leverage is above management's target range. Cash generation is uneven and the covenant tests cannot be checked.
Net debt to pro forma adjusted EBITDA was 3.1x at Q2 FY2027, above the 2.0x to 3.0x target range, as EBITDA fell and shares were repurchased.
Trailing twelve month pro forma adjusted EBITDA fell to 381.3 from 413.0 at the prior year end, and six month revenue fell 7.2%.
Liquidity is large: 231.0 of cash and 966.7 of unutilized credit, with the revolver maturing December 2029.
Operating cash flow follows working capital: FY2026 inflow of 448.4 included a 246.6 working capital release.
Restructuring charges recur each year and are added back; the net add-back to Q2 FY2027 adjusted EBITDA was 20.2.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: ATS is a long-established, publicly listed Canadian builder of automated manufacturing and assembly systems, with products and services spread over four end markets and a global footprint. For a creditor the central business facts are visibility and cyclicality. Order Backlog of 2,009 at September 27, 2026 and a recurring revenue share that management expects at 25 to 35 percent of trailing twelve month revenue give some protection, but customer capital decisions, the timing of large life sciences programs, tariffs and a fall in revenue have moved earnings down, while management has said it will not meet its prior FY2027 growth and margin goals. The company is in the middle of a restructuring: a transportation reorganization that is repositioning a former end market, a services reorganization, and a multi-phase Fixed Cost Transformation Program with facility closures and a workforce reduction of 300 to 400. These actions are meant to lift margins toward a 15 percent long-term target but cost cash first. There is no leveraged buyout, sponsor or acquisition financing in the sources: the debt arose from earlier note issues and a revolving credit facility amended in December 2025, and the only transaction events in the period are facility sales, share repurchases and restructuring. Ownership is dispersed public equity as far as the pack shows, though the annual information form that would confirm holders is missing. Governance signals are mixed: a new CEO and an interim CFO, a reported material weakness in internal controls, and share buybacks while leverage is above target, set against deleveraging during FY2026. Customer concentration is named as a risk factor but never quantified.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: There is no leveraged buyout, merger, sponsor transaction or acquisition financing in the pack, and the context carries no deal terms. The sources describe corporate actions rather than a single transaction. On debt, the company amended its senior secured credit facility on December 4, 2025, extending maturity to December 4, 2029, with a revolving line of 900.0 and a fully drawn term facility of 150.0, and it incurred transaction costs of 2.6; the facility was utilized at 190.0 at September 27, 2026. The Canadian dollar senior notes of 600.0 at 6.50 percent due August 21, 2032 were placed in two tranches in August and December 2024, and the U.S. dollar senior notes of US$350.0 at 4.125 percent are due December 15, 2028. Neither note series was issued in the period covered by the current or prior fiscal year, and no new debt issue is disclosed in FY2026 or the first half of FY2027 other than draws of 85.0 in FY2026 and 40.0 in Q2 FY2027 reported as proceeds from long-term debt (financial base module). On equity, the company announced a normal course issuer bid in December 2025 allowing purchase of up to 8,225,621 shares, and bought 2,244,461 shares for 61.3 in Q2 FY2027. On assets, two U.S. facilities and one German facility are held for sale as part of the transportation reorganization; after quarter end the company completed the sale of the two U.S. facilities for 71.2 with an estimated gain of about 12.2, with one leased back, to be recognized in Q3 FY2027, and the proceeds are expected to fund restructuring. On operations, the Fixed Cost Transformation Program was announced with Q1 FY2027 results on August 6, 2026. The earlier business acquisitions in FY2025, the companies Heidolph and Paxiom, are named as contributors to growth, but their dates, prices and financing are not in the pack. The legal terms of the notes and credit facility, such as covenant levels and baskets that would govern capacity for dividends, debt incurrence or asset disposals, are described only in general terms because the executed documents are absent.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: ATS Corporation is a moderately leveraged, well-funded industrial automation supplier whose earnings are weakening and whose leverage has moved above its own target. The strongest support is liquidity: C$ 231.0 million of cash and C$ 966.7 million of unutilized credit, a revolver running to December 2029, and a first large principal maturity only in December 2028, alongside four end markets and a C$ 2,009 million backlog. The weakest point is the trend: trailing pro forma adjusted EBITDA of C$ 381.3 million is down from C$ 413.0 million, net debt to EBITDA is 3.1x against a 2.0x to 3.0x target, and cash generation is lumpy. Management expects to stay moderately above the range for the rest of FY2027 [business context, leverage expectation conflict]. On the same figures, net debt of C$ 48.3 million less, or EBITDA of C$ 16.1 million more, would return leverage to 3.0x (calculated here, see Calculations). The pending C$ 71.2 million sale of two U.S. facilities is earmarked by management for restructuring costs, so it should not be assumed to reduce net debt.

This module answers one question: can the pinned source set support the requested work, and what remains blocked. It gives no credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion, and it does not normalize, reconcile or calculate any figure.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The pack can support a financial, business and credit read of ATS through the latest quarter, with limitations. Quarterly disclosure is detailed; audited annual statements, debt notes and covenant terms are not included. | Medium | Annual report exhibits and financing documents are missing, so covenant levels, debt carrying values by instrument and audited annual notes cannot be sourced from this pack. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Reporting is in Canadian dollars, and the periods needed are covered: the latest quarter ended in September 2026 and the prior year ended in March 2026. | Currency and period labels are clear, which lowers the risk of mixing bases. | High |

| Debt, liquidity and covenant compliance are described each quarter, but covenant thresholds and debt carrying values by instrument are not printed. | Covenant headroom cannot be tested against actual limits from this pack. | Medium |

| Management reports a material weakness in internal control, and its disclosure controls were not effective at the latest quarter end. | Reported figures carry extra reliability risk until remediation is shown. | High |

| The annual report is a cover document only; the annual discussion and analysis, audited statements and annual information form are not in the pack. | Fiscal 2026 figures rest on the year-end news release, not on audited filings. | High |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is sufficient for the requested work, with bounded limitations, and no source is blocked. The seven issuer files are all text-extractable, share one reporting entity and one reporting currency, and between them cover the latest quarter, the three quarters before it and the prior fiscal year. The quarterly discussion and analysis documents and the two latest earnings releases carry the debt, liquidity, cash-flow, reconciliation and business narrative that the financial base, business context, credit synthesis and evidence-trace modules need. The principal weaknesses are structural rather than fatal. The annual report in the pack is only the Form 40-F cover document, so the audited fiscal 2026 statements, the annual discussion and analysis and the annual information form are named but absent. No credit agreement, note indenture or other executed financing document is supplied, so covenant levels, definitions and baskets can be read only as management describes them. The interim statements in the releases are primary statements without notes. Management states that disclosure controls were not effective because of a material weakness, which bounds how much weight any single reported figure can carry. Each limitation is carried into the consumer assessments below and into the gaps. Source sufficiency here is separate from completion of downstream analysis.

Notes are not reproduced: [6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:20] "Please refer to complete Interim Condensed Consolidated Financial Statements for supplemental notes". The year-end release has the same limit: [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_ats-pressreleasexfy26q4.htm.jsonl, page:16] "Consolidated Statements of Financial Position (in thousands of Canadian dollars)".

Credit facility and notes are described in MD&A text. The facility consists of [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:26] "a fully drawn $150.0 million secured term credit facility" alongside a revolving line, with [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:26] "$966.7 million of unutilized multipurpose credit, including letters of credit" reported at the latest quarter end. Covenants are named but not quantified: [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:27] "financial covenants including a net debt-to-EBITDA test and an interest coverage test" and [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:27] "At September 27, 2026, all of the covenants were met." No threshold, definition or reported covenant ratio is printed in any source, and the credit agreement is not supplied, so compliance is a management assertion that cannot be tested here. The company-defined leverage ratio is shown as [6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:17] "Net Debt to Pro Forma Adjusted EBITDA 3.1x 2.8x"; whether it matches the credit agreement definition is not shown.

The two note series carry their maturities in text: [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:27] "mature on December 15, 2028" for the U.S. dollar notes and [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:28] "mature on August 21, 2032" for the Canadian dollar notes. Instrument amounts are in the MD&A narrative and the contractual obligations table, which shows principal and interest combined, so principal-only maturity walls need a downstream calculation with stated limits.

Letters of credit outside the credit facility are disclosed: [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:29] "the total value of outstanding letters of credit was approximately $274.4 million". Their split among facilities needs the figures at [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:26] and the additional letter of credit facilities, which is a downstream task.

Control environment: [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:37] "disclosure controls and procedures were not effective as of September 27, 2026, due to the material weakness". The Q3 FY2026 text speaks of weaknesses in the plural: [6-K-EX-99.1_2025-12-28_ats-mdaxfy26q3.htm.jsonl, page:31] "address the identified material weaknesses". The later sources use the singular, and the annual MD&A that would explain the change is not in the pack.

Subsequent event inside the cutoff: [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:13] "Subsequent to quarter end, the Company completed the sale of the two U.S. facilities for consideration of $71.2 million". Its accounting is described as falling in the following quarter, so no statements in the pack reflect it.
### Conflicts and superseded statements
| Item | Earlier locator | Later locator | Downstream effect |

| Leverage versus target range | [6-K-EX-99.5_2026-06-28_ats-pressreleasexfy27q1.htm.jsonl, page:6] "management expects the Company to continue to operate within its targeted leverage ratio of 2.0 to 3.0 times throughout fiscal 2027" | [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:6] "slightly above the targeted range of 2.0 to 3.0 times" | A later management update, not a document conflict. Use the Q2 FY2027 statement for the current view and carry the Q1 FY2027 statement as the earlier expectation. Both stay as separate sources; the later one does not delete the earlier. |
No conflicting figure was found between the overlapping Q2 FY2027 MD&A and release in the areas read, but no systematic cross-check was done in this module, and none is claimed.
### Extraction fidelity and parse gaps

Text extraction succeeded for all seven files; extraction success is not a fidelity review. Tables arrive as flattened text lines, so column alignment must be confirmed against the header lines on the same page. Charts and images are not retained: the Q2 FY2027 MD&A shows the heading [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:6] "ORDER BOOKINGS BY QUARTER" with no chart data after it. The quarterly series that the chart presumably depicts is available as text in the results table at [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:31], so the gap is bounded, but no image inspection is claimed. There are no workbooks, scans or slide decks in the pack, and no speaker notes.

Page coverage by source (chunks of extracted text): 9, 42, 29, 45, 51, 30 and 34 pages for the seven files, totalling 240 pages. All pages were searched by term for debt, liquidity, covenant, rating, subsequent-event, control and statement content; the pages cited above were read in full. This is a search-based review, and a page-by-page reading of every narrative page is left to the modules that need them.
## Calculations

No new calculation was performed. This module does not normalize, reconcile or derive figures, and every figure above is quoted verbatim from a cited span. The only arithmetic is the page count: 9 + 42 + 29 + 45 + 51 + 30 + 34 = 240 pages across seven issuer files (inputs from the page index of each pinned source).

Calculations deferred to later modules, with their inputs located: liquidity (cash at [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:24] "Cash and cash equivalents $ 231.0 $ 285.0", facility availability at [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:26]), maturity wall (contractual obligations at [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:28]), and leverage (net debt reconciliation at [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:34]). Principal and interest are combined in the obligations table, and some facilities are in foreign currencies, so those calculations need explicit conversion and perimeter notes.

| G10 | Post-quarter facility sale of the two U.S. facilities is not yet in any statements | Low | Financial base | Treat as a subsequent event with its stated gain estimate and timing |
## Next module

Proceed with the financial base module next, then business and transaction context, credit synthesis and evidence-trace validation, in that dependency order. Pass forward these instructions: use Canadian dollars; label every figure by period (Q2 FY2027, six months FY2027, Q4 FY2026, FY2026, trailing twelve months as management defines it); take current liquidity, debt and covenant statements from the Q2 FY2027 MD&A and keep the Q1 FY2027 leverage statement as the earlier expectation; take full-year FY2026 statements from the Q4 release and state that audit status is not shown in the pack; treat covenant compliance as a management assertion with no thresholds; carry the material weakness and the absent annual exhibits as limitations in every conclusion; and state Not supplied for guarantor names, ratings and legal documents rather than inferring them.

### Financial base view

ATS Corporation entered Q2 FY2027 with a moderately levered balance sheet that is drifting the wrong way. The company's own measure, net debt to pro forma adjusted EBITDA, rose from 2.8x at March 31, 2026 to 3.1x at September 27, 2026, because trailing twelve month adjusted EBITDA fell while net debt rose, helped along by a share repurchase of 61.3 under the normal course issuer bid. Management now expects to operate above its 2.0x to 3.0x target range for the rest of FY2027. Earnings pressure is volume driven: six month FY2027 revenues fell 7.2% year over year (1,359.5 against 1,465.2) and Q2 FY2027 revenues fell while Order Bookings rose, so backlog of 2,009 supports near-term revenue but at a lower margin. Debt service looks comfortable on cash interest cover of 4.18x for the trailing twelve months, and liquidity is large relative to the debt wall: the senior secured revolver runs to December 2029, and the first large principal maturity on the disclosed instruments is the U.S. dollar senior notes in December 2028. The quality of the numbers deserves care. Cash flow in FY2026 was flattered by a large working capital release, adjusted EBITDA adds back restructuring charges that recur every year, the covenant tests are described but not quantified, the interim statements arrive without notes, and management reports a material weakness in internal control. The view is therefore moderate leverage, strong liquidity, deteriorating earnings and incomplete covenant evidence.

### Source context and perimeter

All figures are ATS Corporation consolidated, IFRS, C$. Narrative tables in the MD&A and releases are in millions of dollars; primary statements are in thousands. The balance sheet dates are instants and carry no start date. Flow periods: Q2 FY2027 is the three months ended September 27, 2026 (starting after the Q1 end of June 28, 2026) and the six months run from the April 1 start of the fiscal year (inferred from the March 31 year end); the prior-year comparatives end September 28, 2025; FY2026 is the year ended March 31, 2026. The cover document confirms the registrant and accounting basis: [40-F_2026-03-31_ats-20260331_d2.htm.jsonl, page:6] "Unless otherwise indicated, all dollar amounts in this Annual Report are in Canadian dollars." and [40-F_2026-03-31_ats-20260331_d2.htm.jsonl, page:6] "in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards as issued by".

Interim statements are condensed and unaudited: [6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:19] "Interim Condensed Consolidated Statements of Financial Position (in thousands of Canadian dollars - unaudited)". The year-end statements in the Q4 release carry no audit label in the release, and the audited statements are an absent exhibit; their audit status is therefore not shown in the pack. Notes are not reproduced: [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_ats-pressreleasexfy26q4.htm.jsonl, page:17] "Please refer to complete Consolidated Financial Statements for supplemental notes".

Market taxonomy changed between years: FY2026 reports Consumer Products and Transportation separately ([6-K-EX-99.1_2026-03-31_ats-pressreleasexfy26q4.htm.jsonl, page:12] "Transportation 26.6 68.4 169.7 331.8") while FY2027 reports a combined Industrial and Consumer line ([6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:13] "Industrial & Consumer 136.4 178.2 312.0 362.4"). Adjusted EBITDA is adjusted earnings from operations plus depreciation and amortization; pro forma adjusted EBITDA adds full contribution from recent acquisitions: [6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:22] "Pro forma adjusted EBITDA is adjusted EBITDA on a pro forma basis to reflect full contribution from recent acquisitions." The company excludes restructuring, acquisition costs, cancelled contract costs, legal settlements and certain items that "would be non-recurring in nature" ([6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:22] "certain other adjustments which would be non-recurring in nature"). Six months FY2026 operating cash flow also benefited from a customer settlement: [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:24] "collection of the settlement amount with an electric vehicle". Six months FY2027 operating cash flow fell to 70.3 with working capital contributing only 1.1; Q1 FY2027 operating cash flow was negative ([6-K-EX-99.1_2026-06-28_ats-mdaxfy27q1.htm.jsonl, page:20] "Operating activities (10.3) 155.8") and Q2 FY2027 recovered to 80.7 as working capital released 46.7. Free cash flow for six months FY2027 was 36.5 against 149.6 a year earlier, while net income was a loss of 5.3. Cash interest paid was close to net finance costs (43.3 against 42.9 for six months FY2027), and the share repurchase of 61.3 in Q2 FY2027 consumed more than the entire six month free cash flow. Capital expenditure guidance for FY2027 is 60 to 80 ([6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:25] "between $60 million and $80 million"). ## Calculations
A dagger (†) in a table marks a figure calculated here from cited inputs rather than printed in a source.

C1. Debt components and leverage. Total debt = bank indebtedness + current portion of long-term debt + long-term debt + current lease liabilities + long-term lease liabilities (the components of the company's net debt). Net debt = total debt − cash. EBITDA = trailing twelve month pro forma adjusted EBITDA as printed. - Net debt change since March 31, 2026: 1,192.2 − 1,151.2 = 41.0; EBITDA change 381.3 − 413.0 = −31.7.

- Limitation: trailing figures use the prior-year comparatives in the same filings; the classification of cash interest (operating or financing; whether lease interest is included) is Not supplied.

C3. Liquidity at Sep 27, 2026. Revolver drawn = Credit Facility utilized 190.0 − term loan 150.0 = 40.0 (consistent with proceeds from long-term debt of 40.0 in Q2 FY2027, [6-K-EX-99.5_2026-09-27_ats-pressreleasexfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:21]). Undrawn revolver = 900.0 − 40.0 = 860.0. Unused other facilities = 111.6 − 4.2 = 107.4. Facility build = 860.0 + 107.4 = 967.4 against the company's 966.7 (difference 0.7). Liquidity = 231.0 + 966.7 = 1,197.7 (company figure) or 231.0 + 967.4 = 1,198.4 (facility build). Letters of credit on the revolver: nil, so no deduction.

C4. Indicative conversion of the U.S. Senior Notes: US$350.0 × 1.414 (period-end rate, [6-K-EX-99.1_2026-09-27_ats-mdaxfy27q2.htm.jsonl, page:31]) = C$494.9. The difference of 12.5 is unreconciled; the direction is consistent with unamortized transaction fees net of the 1.3 premium but this is not verified without the debt note.

C6. Add-backs and working capital share. Net add-back = adjusted EBITDA − EBITDA: Q2 FY2027 80.7 − 60.5 = 20.2 (25.0% of adjusted); six months FY2027 173.4 − 124.9 = 48.5 (28.0%); FY2026 413.0 − 362.7 = 50.3 (12.2%). Working capital share of FY2026 operating cash flow = 246.587 / 448.383 = 55.0%. Net debt ex repurchase: (1,192.2 − 61.3) / 381.3 = 2.97x, consistent with management's 3.0x.

C7. Capital expenditure (property, plant and equipment plus intangibles): Q2 FY2027 8.2 + 10.0 = 18.2; six months FY2027 16.2 + 17.6 = 33.8; FY2026 33.6 + 43.1 = 76.7; FY2025 34.0 + 44.1 = 78.1. ### Business and transaction view

ATS is a long-established, publicly listed Canadian builder of automated manufacturing and assembly systems, with products and services spread over four end markets and a global footprint. For a creditor the central business facts are visibility and cyclicality. Order Backlog of 2,009 at September 27, 2026 and a recurring revenue share that management expects at 25 to 35 percent of trailing twelve month revenue give some protection, but customer capital decisions, the timing of large life sciences programs, tariffs and a fall in revenue have moved earnings down, while management has said it will not meet its prior FY2027 growth and margin goals. The company is in the middle of a restructuring: a transportation reorganization that is repositioning a former end market, a services reorganization, and a multi-phase Fixed Cost Transformation Program with facility closures and a workforce reduction of 300 to 400. These actions are meant to lift margins toward a 15 percent long-term target but cost cash first. There is no leveraged buyout, sponsor or acquisition financing in the sources: the debt arose from earlier note issues and a revolving credit facility amended in December 2025, and the only transaction events in the period are facility sales, share repurchases and restructuring. Ownership is dispersed public equity as far as the pack shows, though the annual information form that would confirm holders is missing. Governance signals are mixed: a new CEO and an interim CFO, a reported material weakness in internal controls, and share buybacks while leverage is above target, set against deleveraging during FY2026. Customer concentration is named as a risk factor but never quantified.

## Findings
### Reader summary

Covenant headroom cannot be verified. | Medium | Covenant levels, the credit agreement, audited annual notes and ownership detail are not in the pack, so headroom and structural priority are unverified. |

### Credit view

ATS Corporation is a moderately leveraged, well-funded industrial automation supplier whose earnings are weakening and whose leverage has moved above its own target. The strongest support is liquidity: C$ 231.0 million of cash and C$ 966.7 million of unutilized credit, a revolver running to December 2029, and a first large principal maturity only in December 2028, alongside four end markets and a C$ 2,009 million backlog. The weakest point is the trend: trailing pro forma adjusted EBITDA of C$ 381.3 million is down from C$ 413.0 million, net debt to EBITDA is 3.1x against a 2.0x to 3.0x target, and cash generation is lumpy. The outcome turns on whether the Fixed Cost Transformation Program savings arrive and backlog converts before further buybacks or working capital absorb cash, and on covenant terms nobody outside the company can see in this pack.
### Credit assessment and thesis

Category: Analyst Interpretation. Confidence: Medium, held below High because the business context was ready only with limitations and the covenant, ownership and guarantor evidence is missing. Basis: financial base leverage, liquidity and cash flow rows; business context profile, operating model, governance and credit translation rows.

Thesis: ATS Corporation can service and refinance its debt from a large liquidity cushion and a diversified backlog, but its credit quality depends on stabilizing earnings and returning leverage to range, which the current evidence does not yet show.
### Key findings

1. Leverage is above target and rising (Documentary Fact). Net debt to pro forma adjusted EBITDA was 3.1x at September 27, 2026 against 2.8x at March 31, 2026 and 3.0x at December 28, 2025, with the company's own range at 2.0x to 3.0x [financial base, leverage chart and finding on leverage]. Net debt rose by C$ 41.0 million to C$ 1,192.2 million while trailing EBITDA fell by C$ 31.7 million, partly because ATS spent C$ 61.3 million on share repurchases; excluding them management puts leverage at 3.0x. Management expects to stay moderately above the range for the rest of FY2027 [business context, leverage expectation conflict]. On the same figures, net debt of C$ 48.3 million less, or EBITDA of C$ 16.1 million more, would return leverage to 3.0x (calculated here, see Calculations). The pending C$ 71.2 million sale of two U.S. facilities is earmarked by management for restructuring costs, so it should not be assumed to reduce net debt.

2. Liquidity is strong and the maturity wall is distant (Documentary Fact, with Analyst Interpretation on the risk). ATS holds C$ 231.0 million of cash and C$ 966.7 million of unutilized credit, giving C$ 1,197.7 million. The secured revolver of C$ 900.0 million matures December 4, 2029, and letters of credit of about C$ 274.4 million sit on separate facilities and do not reduce it [financial base, liquidity build]. The first large principal maturity on disclosed instruments is the US$ 350.0 million 4.125% senior notes in December 2028, hedged only in part and only to December 2027, followed by the C$ 600.0 million 6.50% notes in August 2032. Refinancing risk is therefore concentrated in the FY2029 notes and the FY2030 credit facility expiry rather than in the next twelve months.

3. Earnings are falling on volume and mix (Documentary Fact). Six month revenues fell 7.2% and Q2 FY2027 adjusted EBITDA margin was 12.1% against 14.2%, while Order Bookings rose 12.7% to C$ 827 million [financial base; business context operating model]. The backlog of C$ 2,009 million is 2.9% lower than a year earlier, with industrial and consumer backlog at C$ 312 million against C$ 431 million. Management no longer expects its prior FY2027 revenue growth and margin goals and guides Q3 FY2027 revenue to C$ 640 million to C$ 680 million. The risk mechanic is operating leverage: a fixed cost base on lower volumes compresses margins faster than revenue, which lowers the EBITDA that covenants and leverage ratios are measured on.

4. Adjusted EBITDA flatters earning power (Analyst Interpretation on documentary add-back data). The net add-back from EBITDA to adjusted EBITDA was C$ 20.2 million in Q2 FY2027, 25.0% of adjusted EBITDA, and restructuring charges have been added back in FY2025, FY2026 and the first half of FY2027 [financial base, add-back review]. The credit agreement definition of EBITDA is not available, so covenant EBITDA may be higher or lower. Creditors should treat the C$ 381.3 million as an upper bound for recurring earnings until restructuring stops recurring.

5. Cash flow is dominated by working capital timing (Documentary Fact). FY2026 operating cash flow of C$ 448.4 million included a C$ 246.6 million working capital release, 55.0% of the total; six month FY2027 operating cash flow was C$ 70.3 million and free cash flow C$ 36.5 million against C$ 149.6 million a year earlier, when an EV customer settlement was collected [financial base, cash flow quality]. Debt reduction capacity therefore moves with project billing, and restructuring provisions point to cash costs still to come.

6. Cover is adequate today (Documentary Fact with calculation). Trailing EBITDA to cash interest paid is 4.18x against 4.24x for FY2026, helped by lower debt and net finance costs of C$ 42.9 million for six months against C$ 50.0 million. A forward swap fixes the term loan at 3.264% from November 4, 2026; floating exposure on the revolver and the end of the cross-currency hedge in December 2027 are sensitivities [financial base, instruments].

7. Business risk is moderate and visibility is reasonable but not strong (Documentary Fact and Management Language). Four end markets, three regions and a backlog of C$ 2,009 million support revenue visibility, and management targets recurring revenue of 25% to 35% of trailing revenue, a figure not yet reported and so treated as Management Language [business context, operating model]. Offsetting this, project timing is lumpy, tariffs under Section 338 delayed non-life-sciences orders from late August 2026 (partly eased by late October modifications), and cross-border equipment sales into the U.S. were just over 20% of FY2026 adjusted revenues.

8. Governance signals are mixed (Analyst Interpretation). ATS reduced net debt between March 2025 and March 2026, a supportive record, but repurchased shares at above-target leverage, changed CEO and has had an interim CFO since February 2026 [business context, governance table]. Disclosure controls were not effective at September 27, 2026 because of a material weakness, so every reported figure carries added reliability risk. No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed and no creditor-adverse action is described in the sources reviewed, which is a statement about the pack rather than proof.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Liquidity depth (Documentary Fact): C$ 231.0 million cash plus C$ 966.7 million unutilized credit against a modest near-term maturity profile, with the revolver expiring in December 2029. Diversification (Documentary Fact): four end markets and three regions, with life sciences holding the largest backlog at C$ 1,238 million. Backlog and recurring revenue ambition (Documentary Fact and Management Language): C$ 2,009 million of backlog supports near-term revenue, and services growth is a stabilizer. Deleveraging record (Documentary Fact): net debt to EBITDA fell from 3.9x at March 31, 2025 to 2.8x at March 31, 2026 before the recent reversal. Interest cover (Documentary Fact with calculation): 4.18x on trailing cash interest. Restructuring programme (Management Language, qualified): management targets C$ 65 million to C$ 75 million of annualized savings, which is a claim and not yet a result.

Weaknesses. Leverage above target (Documentary Fact): 3.1x against 2.0x to 3.0x, with management expecting to remain above range through FY2027. Falling earnings (Documentary Fact): trailing pro forma adjusted EBITDA C$ 381.3 million down from C$ 413.0 million, and revenue and margin goals withdrawn. Earnings quality (Analyst Interpretation): recurring restructuring add-backs of C$ 20.2 million in the latest quarter. Cash flow volatility (Documentary Fact): FY2026 relied on a C$ 246.6 million working capital release. Capital allocation (Analyst Interpretation): C$ 61.3 million of buybacks while leverage was above range. Control environment (Documentary Fact): material weakness and ineffective disclosure controls, with a new CEO and an interim CFO. Missing structure (Insufficient Information): no covenant levels, no credit agreement or indentures, no guarantor names, no customer concentration figures and no ownership detail, so covenant headroom, priority of claims and single-customer risk cannot be assessed.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Basis |

| Further leverage drift | Lower EBITDA, buybacks and restructuring cash costs lift net debt to EBITDA from 3.1x | Less room before covenant and rating pressure; refinancing terms may worsen | Material | Financial base leverage rows; business context governance rows |

| Covenant breach risk that cannot be tested | Net debt to EBITDA and interest coverage tests exist but levels and definitions are unknown | A breach would restrict the C$ 860.0 million undrawn revolver, the core of liquidity | Material | Financial base covenant section; gap G1 |

| Earnings shortfall versus plan | Tariffs, order timing and mix cut volume while fixed costs stay | Debt service capacity falls; savings program must offset | Material | Financial base add-back review; business context credit translations |
| Cash flow reversal | Working capital builds as bookings convert, offsetting EBITDA | Free cash flow turns weak; debt reduction stalls | Material | Financial base cash flow quality |

| Refinancing concentration in FY2029 and FY2030 | US$ 350.0 million notes (December 2028) and C$ 190.0 million facility drawings (December 2029) fall due close together | Market access and pricing in 2028 and 2029 decide refinancing cost | Material | Financial base debt instruments |
| Reporting reliability | Material weakness and interim CFO | Reported estimates may be revised; credit metrics less reliable | Material | Business context governance; financial base data quality |

| Structural priority unknown | Guarantor names, security of the notes and covenant baskets not supplied | Cannot say how claims rank or how much value can leak | Minor | Business context ownership rows; gap G2 |
## Calculations

No source figure was recalculated; amounts are quoted from the handoffs. One new calculation, using financial base inputs (net debt C$ 1,192.2 million; trailing pro forma adjusted EBITDA C$ 381.3 million; target ceiling 3.0x):
- Net debt consistent with 3.0x at current EBITDA: 3.0 × 381.3 = 1,143.9; reduction needed 1,192.2 − 1,143.9 = 48.3.
- EBITDA consistent with 3.0x at current net debt: 1,192.2 / 3.0 = 397.4; increase needed 397.4 − 381.3 = 16.1.
- Both use the company's own net debt and EBITDA definitions, not the credit agreement's, and ignore changes in lease liabilities and exchange rates.
## Gaps
| ID | Gap | What it affects | Severity | Action |

| G1 | Covenant levels, definitions and reported ratios not supplied; credit agreement and indentures absent | Headroom and liquidity access cannot be assessed | Material | Obtain the executed documents |

| G2 | Names of issuers, co-issuers and guarantors, security of the notes, restricted group not supplied | Priority of claims and leakage capacity | Material | Obtain indentures and the annual information form |

| G3 | Audited FY2026 statements, annual MD&A, debt note and statement notes absent; material weakness reported | Reliability and completeness of the financial base | Material | Obtain annual report exhibits and track remediation |
| G4 | Ownership, customer concentration and acquisition history not disclosed | Concentration and alignment judgments | Minor | Obtain the annual information form |
| G5 | Business context readiness for this module is ready with limitations only; confidence is therefore held below High | Confidence of the whole assessment | Minor | Clear G2 and G4 |
| G6 | Ratings, quotes and peer data not in the context | Market context absent; relative value out of scope | Minor | Not needed for this pathway |

| G7 | Unutilized credit differs by C$ 0.7 million between the company figure and the facility build; status and expiry of other facilities (C$ 111.6 million) not stated | Liquidity may be marginally overstated | Minor | Obtain facility details |
## Next module

Proceed to the evidence trace validation. Claims to test against the earlier handoffs: leverage of 3.1x against a 2.0x to 3.0x range; liquidity of C$ 1,197.7 million; trailing pro forma adjusted EBITDA of C$ 381.3 million; cash interest cover of 4.18x; the C$ 246.6 million working capital release; the net add-back of C$ 20.2 million; and the calculation that C$ 48.3 million less net debt or C$ 16.1 million more EBITDA restores the 3.0x ceiling. Keep the conflicts and gaps above in the trace.
